question: Which is the first Indian state/UT to launch the nPROUD (New Programme for Removal of Unused Drugs) project?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** became the first Indian state/UT to launch the **nPROUD (New Programme for Removal of Unused Drugs)** project. This initiative was undertaken to tackle the issue of unused or expired drugs being improperly disposed of, leading to environmental and public health concerns.
 
• The program aims to create a comprehensive system for the **collection and safe disposal of unused or expired medications** from households and institutions. It ensures that these drugs are not discarded irresponsibly or misused.
 
• **Environmental concerns** are a primary focus of this initiative, as improperly disposed medications often contaminate water bodies and soil, causing harm to ecosystems.
 
• The state government collaborated with various stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, pharmaceutical companies, and waste management bodies, to implement the program effectively.
 
• The **nPROUD project** highlights Kerala's proactive approach in addressing public health and environmental challenges, setting an example for other states and UTs to follow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of the nPROUD Project:**

 
 
• **Environmental Protection:** Improper disposal of medicines often leads to contamination of water bodies and soil, disrupting ecosystems and causing bioaccumulation in aquatic life.
 
• **Public Health:** Expired or unused medicines in households pose risks of accidental ingestion, misuse, or abuse, particularly among children and vulnerable populations.
 
• **Safe Disposal:** The initiative promotes eco-friendly and safe disposal methods, reducing the potential risks associated with pharmaceuticals entering the waste stream.
 
 
 
• **Steps Taken Under the nPROUD Project:**
 
 
• Setting up of collection points at pharmacies, hospitals, and healthcare centers for easy disposal of unused drugs.
 
• Awareness campaigns to educate the public about the importance of proper drug disposal and the harmful effects of improper practices.
 
• Collaboration with pharmaceutical companies for reverse logistics and safe incineration of collected drugs.
 
 
 
• **Other Initiatives Addressing Drug Disposal:**
 
 
• Globally, countries like the **United States** and **Canada** have similar programs such as the **Drug Take-Back Initiative** to ensure safe and proper disposal of medications.
 
• In India, this is one of the pioneering projects, and its success could lead to similar initiatives in other states and UTs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why is Proper Disposal of Medicines Important?**

 
 
• **Environmental Risks:** Pharmaceuticals in water bodies can harm aquatic life and interfere with natural ecosystems.
 
• **Health Concerns:** Accidental ingestion or misuse of expired drugs can lead to poisoning or adverse health effects.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Role in Public Health and Environmental Protection:**
 
 
• Kerala has often been at the forefront of innovative health and environmental initiatives, such as the **Haritha Keralam Mission**, which focuses on sustainable development and waste management.
 
• The nPROUD project complements Kerala's broader efforts to promote environmental sustainability and public health.
